summary: Explains that the Tao of the IETF, previously published as a series of RFCs, is instead to be published as a web page. It also sets out the procedure for publishing and editing that page. It is informational. It was replaced by RFC 9592.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 6722 explains how the Tao of the IETF moved from a series of RFCs to a web page that could be updated more easily. It sets out how changes are proposed, reviewed, published, and archived; RFC 9592 later replaced this procedure.

subtitle: How the Tao of the IETF moved from RFCs to a maintained web page.

tldr.problem: The Tao of the IETF was published as an RFC, while the community wanted a version that could be updated more easily.
tldr.mechanism: The Tao becomes a web page edited by people designated by the IESG, with proposed changes reviewed by the IESG and published by the IETF Secretariat.
tldr.outcome: RFC 6722 obsoleted RFC 4677 and was later obsoleted by RFC 9592.

facts.label: Editors
facts.value: One or more, designated by the IESG

today: RFC 6722 is Informational and was obsoleted by RFC 9592.

sections.title: From RFC to Web Page
sections.content:
The Tao describes IETF meetings and Working Groups, related organizations, and the standards process. It is an informational overview, not a formal process document. It had traditionally been published as an RFC.

RFC 6722 describes publishing the Tao as a web page that can be updated more easily. It obsoletes RFC 4677 because the web page becomes the latest version of the Tao.
sections.plainLanguage: The Tao is an overview of how the IETF works. This memo moves its publication from RFCs to a web page that can be revised more easily.

sections.title: Editing, Review, and Publication
sections.content:
The IESG designates one or more editors. People suggest changes on the tao-discuss mailing list. The editor decides which proposals to submit to the IESG for approval and publishes a proposed revision for review.

The IESG may accept proposed changes and submits the changed version to the IETF Secretariat for publication. Each published version has a visible timestamp, and the versions are archived using dates in their URLs. The RFC says translated versions do not represent IETF consensus.
sections.plainLanguage: Editors collect and prepare suggestions, and the IESG decides which changes to approve. The Secretariat publishes approved changes, and dated copies are kept in an archive.

sections.title: The Agreed Publication Approach
sections.content: Discussion considered a simple web page, periodic RFC snapshots, and wiki approaches with different editing permissions. The procedure in this RFC was the rough consensus of that discussion. The memo also says that how translations are recorded and archived is outside its scope.
sections.plainLanguage: The community considered several ways to publish and edit the Tao. The chosen process combines a web page with editor and IESG review.

references.text: Hoffman, P. and S. Harris, "The Tao of IETF - A Novice's Guide to the Internet Engineering Task Force", BCP 17, RFC 4677, September 2006.
